newsitem.title: USA: Jones buys New Mexico cable system for $223 million.
newsitem.headline: Jones buys New Mexico cable system for $223 million.

text.p: Jones Intercable Inc. said Thursday it agreed to buy an Albuquerque cable television system from Cable TV Fund 12-BCD Venture for about $223 million.
Jones, which is the venture's general partner, said it would use its existing credit lines to pay for the acquisition, which it expects to close in the first quarter of 1998.
The Englewood, Colo.-based cable television operator said the Albuquerque system serves about 112,800 viewers.

"The acquisition of the Albuquerque system is yet another step toward our goal of becoming an owned-asset company, rather than primarily a management company," Jones President James O'Brien said in a statement.
Jones said Wednesday it planned a secondary offering of 7.8 million shares to help pay for buying an Independence, Mo., cable system from one of its managing partnerships.
Jones Intercable, Inc. is one of the largest cable television operators in the United States. It owns or manages cable operations serving approximately 1.4 million customers in 17 states.
Jones stock was unchanged at $12.625 in morning trading on Nasdaq.
